items.summary: In an interview published Tuesday with the South China Morning Post, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said that new U.S. export curbs on advanced AI chips aimed at restricting their use by China will not deter Malaysia from working with Beijing and Chinese firms. The comments came ahead of his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping during last week's APEC summit in Shenzhen. Anwar told the South China Morning Post that Malaysia is not leaning toward either China or the United States, though he found it generally easier to deal with Beijing due to existing cultural and regional ties. He added that China has not raised concerns over Kuala Lumpur's relationship with the U.S. or its technology arrangements with Washington, dismissing suggestions that he was tilting toward China as untrue. The new U.S. rule restricts shipments of advanced chips to Southeast Asian countries such as Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, which Chinese companies have used to access computing power to train AI models. Anwar said Malaysia would monitor whether any U.S.-linked companies were shipping chips to China, just as it monitors Chinese firms required to operate under rules set by Beijing, noting that conditions on a company not exporting to China are fair but will not preclude decisions to work with Chinese investments and companies making their own choices. He also said Malaysia would seek financing from foreign investors seeking government assistance to safeguard its supply chain, stating the country is getting smarter as a business.
items.title: Malaysia's PM Anwar: US Chip Sanctions Won't Deter Malaysia-China Tech Ties

items.summary:
Satyaki Savarkar, the paternal grandnephew of freedom fighter Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, has sent a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi demanding an unconditional apology and correction over remarks about his ancestor in her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love. The notice was issued by advocate Sangram Kolhatkar on Satyaki's behalf and requires the demands be met within 15 days, warning that non-compliance could lead to legal proceedings before a competent court or authority.

The objection centers on two statements in the book. On page 201, the memoir states that while Congress freedom fighters endured British imprisonment, RSS ideologues like Savarkar were writing mercy petitions and colluding with colonial authorities as informers. Satyaki alleges this creates an unsupported impression of collaboration or informing against Indian freedom fighters, disputing it on historical grounds including Savarkar's prolonged imprisonment in the Cellular Jail in the Andaman Islands.

On page 443, the book describes Savarkar as articulating a vision viewing India primarily as a nation where Hindus are supreme—an outlook attributed to Hindutva and the Sangh Parivar. The notice argues this oversimplifies his political philosophy and should be considered within its proper historical, intellectual, and political context.

The two statements together allegedly present a distorted account of Savarkar's role in the freedom struggle and mislead readers about his legacy. To support Savarkar's stature as a patriot, the notice cites government recognition during former prime minister Indira Gandhi's tenure, including a commemorative postage stamp issued in his honor and her personal contribution of Rs 11,000 from her bank account toward the Swatantryaveer Savarkar Rashtriya Smarak. It asks Sonia to explain how these statements reconcile with such records.

The notice demands an unconditional apology plus public clarification explaining the historical basis, context, and intended meaning of the statements, along with acknowledgment and correction of any inaccuracies or misleading implications. It also requests that appropriate steps be taken in consultation with HarperCollins Publishers India—Sonia Gandhi's publisher—to correct, qualify, or withdraw the objectionable statements from subsequent editions, reprints, and electronic versions.

The memoir was reportedly released on November 10, and Satyaki said he recently came across it before being disturbed by the statements concerning his ancestor. PTI reported on the notice.
items.title: Savarkar's Grandnephew Serves Legal Notice to Sonia Gandhi Over Memoir Remarks

items.summary: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) of India's Union Home Ministry anti-cybercrime wing, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), issued an advisory on Monday warning that a logged-in WhatsApp Web session left open on a public computer or shared device could allow cybercriminals to hijack accounts. The unit said such sessions could be used to gain unauthorized access and let malicious actors read private messages, send communications while impersonating the account holder, view contact lists and group conversations, and exploit the user's trusted identity to carry out fraud, phishing and social-engineering attacks. I4C cautioned that simply closing a browser window or tab does not end an authenticated session, advising users instead to manually log out after each use—particularly on office computers, shared systems, public devices, cyber cafes, kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed computers or other untrusted machines—and to avoid conducting official, sensitive work involving government, organizational, financial or confidential information through WhatsApp Web. When use is unavoidable, the unit recommended using incognito and private browsing modes, keeping devices, operating systems and browsers secure with updated security software while avoiding suspicious downloads, unknown files and cracked software, and treating unexpected messages sent from an account or unusual replies as serious signs of compromise.
items.title: India's I4C Warns WhatsApp Web Sessions Can Enable Account Hijacking

items.summary:
The Supreme Court on Monday directed that priority be given to appeals from 22 lakh people, out of a total of 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll. The court sought the state government's response to allegations that voters deleted during the SIR exercise are being denied ration and benefits under various social welfare schemes.

The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said even among the 22 lakh appeals, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) should be heard ahead of others, given the upcoming civic elections. The court also directed that the Calcutta High Court chief justice, in consultation with the Election Commission, increase the number of tribunals currently at 19 to handle the 38 lakh appeals filed after SIR over deletions related to voters declared absent, shifted, duplicate or dead, or flagged for 'logical discrepancy' connected to mapping. The bench further asked the Election Commission to requisition additional space for housing these tribunals.

The direction followed remarks by advocate Prashant Bhushan, who told the court that of 1.4 lakh appeals decided so far by the tribunals appointed after SIR, more than 90% have been allowed, restoring names in the electoral roll. Bhushan said this was a strong indicator based on a large sample size to persuade the top court to direct those whose names were deleted be permitted to vote in upcoming elections.

Bhushan, supported by senior advocate G Sankaranarayanan, told the court that although it had clarified deletion of electoral roll names would have no consequence beyond voting—including regarding citizenship—the state government has been denying deleted voters ration through the public distribution system (PDS) and benefits under social welfare schemes such as Annapurna Yojana. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta countered these were bald assertions, alleging petitioners had cited no example to substantiate their claims.

The CJI-led bench asked the state government to file a response to the allegations. Separately, the Supreme Court postponed to Wednesday its hearing on the state government's appeal challenging an interim order of a Calcutta High Court division bench that restrained the state Election Commission from announcing a schedule for KMC polls, in which wards were increased from 144 to 209 by an amending Act. Mehta said the high court mistakenly concluded the state government lacked jurisdiction over increasing ward numbers and adjusting boundaries.
items.title: Supreme Court Prioritizes Appeals to Restore West Bengal Voter Names

items.summary: At a United Nations Security Council briefing on Monday, India's Permanent Representative Harish Parvathaneni called for an immediate end to attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Black Sea, stressing that safe navigation through international waterways must be restored amid the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Addressing the high-level session, Ambassador Parvathaneni said the war, now in its fifth year, has far-reaching consequences due to interconnected global supply chains, noting India's readiness to contribute to efforts toward a peaceful resolution and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for moving from 'endless war to the end of war.' He highlighted that armed conflicts disrupt agriculture, displace communities, damage infrastructure, and hinder humanitarian access, with consequences extending globally through disruptions to energy, fertiliser, transport, and agricultural trade while disproportionately impacting the Global South. Parvathaneni emphasized the Security Council's need to prioritise humanitarian access, protection of civilian infrastructure, and freedom of navigation so that humanitarian supplies and legitimate trade are not affected. He underscored the Black Sea region's importance to global food security, noting it and India together account for almost a fifth of global cereal production, while Russia and Ukraine combined accounted for nearly a quarter of global exports of wheat, maize, and barley. The Indian envoy cited India's humanitarian assistance—wheat supplies to Afghanistan, rice to Sudan, and aid to Palestine—and stressed that the Global South is disproportionately affected by food, fuel, and fertiliser crises from conflicts, with energy shortages intensifying concerns; he referenced External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's observation at last month's G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting that fertiliser shortages stem partly from the Black Sea and partly from the Gulf and Red Sea. Parvathaneni recalled the 1943 Bengal famine, which killed over three million people in India, as a reminder of distant conflicts' devastating human costs. He detailed attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea involving four ships: MV Omorfi (attacked July 18), MV Royad Mammadov (October), and MV Golden Leo and MV AGN RAGNAR, resulting in four dead and two missing Indian seafarers; he thanked partner countries for repatriating injured seafarers. Parvathaneni called for an end to targeting commercial shipping and restoration of safe navigation through international waterways at the earliest, noting India's efforts to strengthen maritime safety cooperation, including launching the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers with Liberia during earlier this month's UN high-level week. The voluntary mechanism supports the International Maritime Organisation and International Labour Organisation in addressing shipping safety and security; Parvathaneni said New Delhi is working directly with both sides on Black Sea shipping and grain export corridor safety, reiterating support for an early end to the conflict and 'enduring peace.'
items.title: India Calls for End to Black Sea Shipping Attacks at UN Security Council

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) issued an advisory cautioning investors about the risks of relying on grey market premiums (GMP) to gauge initial public offering prices. Sebi explained that GMP transactions occur before a stock's formal listing, take place outside the exchange framework, are not subject to regulatory oversight, and carry neither settlement guarantees nor investor protection. The regulator also stated that these transactions do not follow any formal price discovery process. In its advisory, Sebi said that publishing such pre-listing premium figures could be detrimental to investors' interests and contrary to transparency and accountability principles in the securities market. Consequently, the regulator called for discontinuing the publication of grey market premium figures through any mode or platform across the securities market.
items.title: Sebi Warns Against Relying on Grey Market Premium as IPO Price Indicator

items.summary: On Monday, Cockroach Janta Party convenor and investigative journalist Saurav Das alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter of Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London at 1 am. In a social media post, Das said he had been invited by prestigious universities including Oxford, Cambridge, LSE (London School of Economics), and Edinburgh to deliver talks on what he called the 'cockroach movement,' which concerns youth protests in India. He stated that an 'anti-intellectual government' was afraid of him traveling to these institutions. Hours later, Cockroach Janta Party leader Ratna Singh said she too had been invited to speak at the Oxford Union but her visa had been rejected a few days earlier; she added that Das's denial raises troubling questions about freedom of expression and space for young voices in India. On Monday, party founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that someone 'in power was jealous' of Das receiving an invitation from the University of Oxford. The Cockroach Janta Party political campaign had named Das as its chief spokesperson on June 3, days ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, then Union education minister, over alleged irregularities in conducting competitive examinations; Pradhan resigned on July 25 after the protest spread to other parts of the country following a police crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi. Das was a key leader of those protests and held discussions with the Union government along with another campaign spokesperson, Ashutosh Ranka. On October 13, Das and Ranka were detained for trespassing on Jantar Mantar and waving the national flag amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in revising the voter roll; they had 'sneaked into' Jantar Mantar to oppose authorities' decision to denotify the area as a designated protest site. They were arrested a day later and released on October 21.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party's Saurav Das Alleges Delhi Airport Stop Before UK Trip

items.summary: In May, a 14-year-old girl named Vaishnavi in the hill hamlet of Peddaporlu developed what is locally called 'chali-jwaram' (chills-fever) after exposure during a storm. Her family initially received only basic treatment at the nearest government Primary Health Centre and declined to travel, as mud roads connecting their village are frequently washed away by torrential rains. After seven days of queuing with blood samples for testing, Vaishnavi was not admitted because the district hospital in Paderu has no overnight facilities; she traveled back and forth three times on a two-wheeler before doctors urged transport to King George Hospital in Visakhapatnam, 106 kilometres away. Her mother said she would prefer taking her daughter to a guru-guniya (local faith healer) who performs animal sacrifices than sending her to the hospital. After spending over Rs 1,000 on fuel across roughly 270 kilometres and around Rs 15,000 for one day's stay at a private hospital in Paderu—while Vaishnavi's family earns about Rs 7,500 per month selling agricultural produce to contractors—she was finally diagnosed with malaria. She later recovered after three days of treatment at the district hospital.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh villages give a reality check to India's 2030 malaria elimination target

The Indian Air Force is expected to take delivery of its first locally manufactured C295 transport aircraft, built jointly by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) and Airbus, with officials reporting the aircraft is undergoing final flight trials and certification as TASL and Airbus target year-end delivery. The plane will join one of the IAF's two existing C295 squadrons based in Agra and Vadodara.

The programme traces to a September 2021 defence ministry contract with Airbus worth ₹21,935 crore for 56 planes aimed at boosting self-reliance in India's defence manufacturing sector. Of the total order, Airbus has delivered 16 aircraft to the IAF in flyaway condition from Spain while the remaining units are being assembled in India; of those remaining, delivery of the first was earlier scheduled for September-end but then-IAF chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh noted in October that minor issues were being resolved. The overall production and delivery programme remains on schedule, with officials stating the remaining 39 aircraft will be delivered by August 2031.

Atmanirbharta (self-reliance) is a key priority for current IAF chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who took over as Chief of the Air Staff on October 31 and outlined his vision using the acronym "VAYU"—V for vigilance and readiness, A for atmanirbharta, Y for yukti (ingenuity), and U for unity of effort. The IAF is expected to begin raising its third C295 squadron next year.

The aircraft will enhance logistics capabilities in forward areas including those near the contested border with China and replace the ageing Avro transport fleet that entered service in the early 1960s. Under the programme, India manufactures more than 13,000 parts and 4,600 sub-assemblies along with all major component assemblies, while Airbus supplies equipment such as engines, landing gear, and avionics; the tactical airlifter is powered by two Pratt & Whitney PW127G turboprop engines. The aircraft can carry up to nine tonnes of payload or 71 personnel or 45 paratroopers at a maximum speed of 480 kmph, operates from short or unprepared airstrips, and has a rear ramp for paradropping troops and cargo.
items.title: IAF to Receive First India-Made C295 Transport Aircraft by December 31

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast isolated heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds across parts of South Peninsular India this week, attributing the activity to easterly waves over the Bay of Bengal and off the Kerala-Karnataka coast. Under troughs in these easterlies, IMD says isolated heavy rainfall is very likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal from 23 to 27 November, and over Kerala and Mahe from 24 to 27 November. Fairly widespread to widespread showers are expected across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry from 24 to 26 November; Kerala and Mahe from 24 to 27 November; and Lakshadweep from 25 to 28 November. The agency has also issued warnings for thunderstorms, lightning, and squally weather across the southern peninsula.

While West and Central India are expected to see largely dry weather during the week, IMD reports that minimum temperatures will fall gradually by 3–5°C over Central India until 26 November, by 3–4°C over East India until 27 November, and by 2–3°C over Northwest India until 28 November. Dense morning fog is very likely in isolated pockets of Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura through 25 November, with dense fog also expected over Assam and Meghalaya on 24 and 25 November.

The Met Department cautioned that reduced visibility from the fog could disrupt airport, highway, and railway operations while posing respiratory and eye-irritation risks. In Delhi-NCR, IMD forecasts mainly clear skies with mist or shallow fog during morning hours through 26 November, moderate fog likely in a few pockets on 25 and 26 November.

For the national capital specifically, IMD says Tuesday (November 24) will feature mainly clear skies with mist or shallow fog in some places during mornings. Daytime maximum temperatures are forecast to hover between 24°C and 26°C—remaining below normal by up to 1.6°C–3.0°C at most places—while minimum temperatures will settle near normal in the 10°C to 12°C range.
items.title: IMD Issues Heavy Rain Alert for Tamil Nadu and Kerala Through November 27

items.summary: Tension and uncertainty prevailed around the Karthigai Deepam lighting at the Tirupparankundram hill shrine in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita limited public assembly and restricted hilltop access. The Supreme Court allowed a restricted one-time lighting of the lamp by authorised officials at 6 PM, barring public access and processions. Following a report identifying the Deepathoon as a British-era survey stone, the state government filed a review petition. Approximately 5,600 police personnel were deployed to manage the situation, while political parties debated the matter and Hindu groups urged adherence to court orders.
items.title: Tension Rises at Tirupparankundram Hill Shrine During Karthigai Deepam Lighting

items.summary: Bihar unit chief of the AIMIM party, Akhtarul Iman, sparked a political controversy with remarks about Muslim bridal traditions. He criticized what he described as the lack of proper veiling during wedding receptions, comparing uncovered brides to courtesans and citing Sharia law's mandate for modesty. His comments were condemned by opposition leaders as sexist and derogatory toward women's dignity. Critics urged party leader Asaduddin Owaisi to respond to the controversy, raising concerns about attitudes toward women's rights and personal freedom.
items.title: AIMIM MLA Akhtarul Iman Draws Criticism Over Comments on Muslim Bridal Practices

items.summary: The Airline Pilots' Association of India (ALPA India) has urged the Civil Aviation Ministry to examine whether SpiceJet's financial difficulties are creating risks for flight safety. In a letter dated November 17, signed by Captain Sam Thomas, President and IFALPA Director of ALPA India, the association raised concerns over delayed salary payments to pilots and cabin crew, pending maintenance organisation and spare-parts supplier payments, and employee pressure during repeated flight disruptions. ALPA warned that financial uncertainty and stress from unpaid salaries could affect the alertness, concentration and decision-making of employees responsible for passenger safety, arguing aviation professionals should not perform safety-critical duties while struggling with basic financial commitments. The association also highlighted difficulties faced by pilots, cabin crew and ground staff during delays, cancellations and other operational disruptions, noting frontline employees increasingly face passenger frustration despite having little control over management decisions causing such disruptions. ALPA flagged the possible impact of financial constraints on aircraft maintenance, warning that payment delays to maintenance organisations, spare-parts suppliers and essential service providers could result in grounded aircraft and further operational disruptions while increasing workload pressure on engineering personnel. The association questioned what it described as the DGCA's apparent double standards in enforcing employment-related regulations, pointing out that the regulator strictly applies Civil Aviation Requirements concerning notice periods and No Objection Certificates when pilots want to leave an airline, yet reportedly tells employees the regulator cannot intervene in contractual matters when airlines delay or fail to pay salaries. ALPA argued that if notice periods are justified for flight safety, persistent non-payment of salaries must equally be recognised as a flight safety concern. The association has asked the Civil Aviation Ministry and DGCA to urgently examine the safety implications of financial distress at SpiceJet and other similarly affected airlines, with demands including closer monitoring of aircraft maintenance resources and payments, timely salary payment to pilots and cabin crew, and a faster release and NOC process when employers have demonstrably failed contractual obligations. The letter was marked to the Director General of Civil Aviation and the Prime Minister's Office. These concerns come amid continuing operational difficulties at SpiceJet, with flight disruptions and passenger complaints adding to questions about the airline's financial and operational position.
items.title: ALPA Warns SpiceJet Financial Troubles Raise Flight Safety Concerns

items.summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced during a Monday media briefing that India's first bullet train is expected to begin trial runs in May 2027 on the 50-km Surat-Bilimora stretch of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor. He said electrification work on the section had been completed, while signalling-related work was targeted for completion by January 2027.
items.title: India's First Bullet Train to Begin Trials in May 2027, Railway Minister Announces
